newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury prints up legal "funny money".
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury prints up legal "funny money".

text.p: The U.S. Treasury Department admitted on Friday that part of its sophisticated effort to foil counterfeiters had gone slightly awry when a manufacturer's error created some $4.7 million in legal "funny money".
Officials said the mix-up occurred on a batch of new $100 bills, when the manufucturer put the high-tech security thread and watermark on the wrong sides of the paper.
If done correctly, the security thread should appear on the left side of the portrait of Benjamin Franklin and the watermark on the right.
"We want to emphasize that the bills are legal tender but if people are uncomfortable, they can bring the bill to their local bank to be exchanged," a Treasury spokesman said.

While officials are far from certain, it appears that about 46,000 of the 890 million new notes were printed on the mistaken paper, although they said 33,000 of these have already been returned from banks.
The government is continuing to search for the notes, and more than likely now they will by joined currency collectors.
